newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 25.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- RETAILERS WARNED SINGLE CURRENCY COULD COST 22BN STG

A research report from Euro-Commerce, the EU retailing body, has estimated that switching to a single currency could leave European Union retailers burdened with over 22bn stg-worth of costs. The report estimates that British retailers would face a bill of 3.5bn stg, equivalent to about 60 stg per person. Lord Blyth, deputy chairman of high street retailer Boots, warned about the inflationary dangers if such a level of costs was passed on to consumers in full.
-- ARGOS WINS VAT REFUND IN EUROPEAN RULING

Catalogue retailer Argos is to be refunded 1.4m stg after the European Court of Justice ruled it had been overtaxed by that amount on special discount offers to customers. The ruling, on whether VAT should be payable on the full original or discounted price, overturns an expert opinion given by the court's own advocate-general in June. Personal products manufacturer Elida Gibbs, which claimed a rebate of 880,000 stg, will also benefit from the ruling.
-- EMAP STEPS UP EFFORTS TO OUST REBELS

The boardroom battle at media group Emap is to rumble on at least until December, when an extraordinary general meeting will be held. The meeting will seek to oust two of Emap's non- executive directors who had earlier called for the resignation of the chairman, Sir John Hoskyns. Now both camps are likely to organise campaigns for shareholder support in the run-up to the EGM.
-- NATIONAL SAVINGS HIT BY BOOKKEEPING ERRORS

The UK's National Savings Agency has been slated in a report from the public spending watchdog the National Audit Office (NAO). The report found that control systems at the agency were so poor it was impossible to tell whether a series of mistakes were due to human or computer error, or fraud.
-- KINNOCK MAY FORCE CUT IN EU AIRFARES

European Union transport commissioner Neil Kinnock has announced a crackdown on high ticket prices across the EU. Kinnock threatened to order airlines to withdraw fares deemed to be too expensive, and said that some of the fares within the EU 'could be described as excessive'. The industry responded angrily to the comments, with David Henderson of the Association of European Airlines suggesting the Commission should look instead at the issue of high costs for airport and other services.
-- COMMISSIONER 'TO LOOK INTO' BSKYB DEAL

The EC competition commissioner Karel Van Miert has said he plans to 'look into' the four-year deal which satellite broadcaster BSkyB has to televise football matches from England's Premier League. Speaking on a BBC radio sports programme, Van Miert expressed concern that as many people as possible are allowed to see sporting events, and added 'we have to question for how long companies are allowed to own these rights'.
-- BAA MAY FUND TERMINAL 5 WITH 230M STG CHARGES

Airports operator British Airports Authority hopes that price controls on landing and take-off charges at its London Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted aiport will provide up to 230m stg of funding for the building of a fifth terminal at Heathrow airport. The price controls were announced on Thursday by the Civil Aviation Authority, which endorsed the recommendations made by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission in July and restricted price rises to no more than three percentage points below inflation over the next five years.
-- PRIMARK IN $105M TAKEOVER OF ICV

US financial information and technology company Primark has announced a takeover deal with British company ICV, which supplies share price data. The takeover will cost the Primark $105m (67m stg) and is linked to a joint venture with US financial information publisher Dow Jones. The new venture, offering historical and real time information about international equities, is expected to challenge similar services from Reuters.
-- PHILIPS TO TAKE Fl 1BN CHARGE FOR OVERHAUL

Cor Boonstra, the new president of Dutch electronics company Philips, has continued his shake-up of the company by ordering the sale of lossmaking units and further pruning of management layers. The drastic overhaul was announced by Boonstra at a press conference called Thursday to announce a 77.2 per cent slide in third quarter net earnings, to Fl 123m. The shake-up will cost Fl 1bn (363m stg).
-- VIRGIN EXPRESS IN SABENA ACCORD

Preparations for a European air battle between British Airways and Virgin Express took another turn on Thursday when Virgin Express, Richard Branson's cut-price European airline, announced it has reached an outline agreement to take over loss-making flights between Brussels and London operated by Belgian airline Sabena. The move follows news earlier this week that British Airways has made a joint takeover bid with French bank Groupe Rivaud for the troubled French carrier Air Liberte. Virgin Express has been approached to make a rival consortium bid for Air Liberte.
